highlights: **Less client work:** Shared tooltips, fewer unchanged sidebar-row renders, lighter command-palette filtering and chat layout, and refreshes limited to visible file-tree folders reduce unnecessary work. Mobile thread switches also commit less; these changes do not establish a measured CPU or memory reduction on this fleet.

**More reliable agent sessions:** Codex and OpenCode recover prompts interrupted by an early Stop, Cursor recovers requests interrupted before their first checkpoint, and Claude Auto mode follows provider availability. Antigravity child work now appears in the normal timeline.

**Android and mobile:** Side chats, subagents and previews open in the Android inspector. Keyboard recreation, photo attachment, copied images, terminal pastes and long links receive fixes, alongside mobile navigation and file-preview improvements.

**Files, workflows and everyday fixes:** EPUB/DOCX and notebook attachment extraction preserves more structure; Markdown links, command output and Unicode truncation receive many correctness fixes. Workflow runs can declare a subject, and automatic pull also keeps unviewed project roots current when enabled.

**Fork controls and privacy retained:** Project snooze and quick-snooze actions now use upstream's shared tooltip implementation. Multi-project filtering, project worktree locations, managed server updates and no-outbound-telemetry behavior remain. Upstream's renamed telemetry environment variables cannot restore analytics; routine local trace sampling is preserved without external exporters.

**Availability is not activation:** Desktop and server releases are offered through the existing updater UI; no fleet server is restarted by publication. Android preview delivery remains an in-place APK update through the existing Syncthing folder, not proof of phone installation.
